questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Exploring a new country in Europe and especially a country with many beautiful natural areas.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was such an amazing experience and I am really thankful for the opportunity to go abroad. Cork is a lovely city and I would definetely recommend everyone going to Ireland to explore the country's (especially the western part) natural areas (Killarney mountains, Dingle Peninsula, Burren national park, Inish islands)!

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was fine - the international office in Cork was super helpful. And the exchange office from KU was also super helpful. It is just quite stressful and confusing before going on exchange as there is a lot to figure out (housing, course registration etc.) but just remember that it will work out in the end! I barely remember all the stress before going on exchange.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The accommodation-office from University College Cork helped me find a student-accommodation.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: They were helpful however, I do think they could have emphasised how critical the housing-crisis is in Cork (and Ireland in general) because I found out quite late compared to the scale of the crisis.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
Very difficult - I cannot emphasise enough that it is quite essential to begin in good time to find an accommodation in Cork. I started searching for an accommodation in April (started in Cork in September) and got my accommodation the day I travelled to Cork. 
Write to the accommodation-office at University College Cork and ask to get on their list for student accommodations. And check their webpage out with their list of student-accommodations. There are many accommodations however many of them are really expensive. 
I would recommend looking for Seven North Mall, Scholar Lee and Brookfield. These are some of the 'cheaper' options. There is also Ashling House, Broga House and Yugo Melbourn point howver, these places are way to expensive to be honest. I have friends who paid 1400€ per month so just start in good time with the search for accommodations.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Housing is super expensive in Cork due to the housing crisis in Ireland and there are many international students searching for them. Living off-campus is fine so long as you live quite central (but most of the student accommodations are place in the centre).

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Just way to expensive and many of the private student accommodations have quite mean landlords (to be honest) that only care about profit. It is quite sad since Cork otherwise is such a lovely city with very sweet people. The housing crisis is bad however I would never have chosen differently - the exchange was absolutely lovely (in my opinion)!

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It is important to search for modules (kurser) in their 'book of modules for visiting students' since not all of their modules are for visiting students. And just be prepared for changes in modules short before the actual exchange since the timetables appear very late in the process (about a week before start). I had to change some modules because of a timetable-conflict.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The international office from University College Cork was there to help and otherwise it was fine to figure it out by myself.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I had to change some classes just before start so sadly I did not get all of the classes I hoped for but it was okay.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just be prepared to change some modules just before start hehe.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I really enjoyed some classes (2 out of 6 classes only) however the other ones I was not super enthusiastic about. I think that their content was quite superficial and not in-depth going about the content of the classes. Maybe because most of the classes are 5 ects-points and you only have 2 hours of lectures per week. Maybe I was also quite unlucky with some of my classes. But the 2 classes I really liked were super interesting and I don't think I could have found them in Copenhagen.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I chose 3rd and 4th year bachelor-level classes and the level was not difficult compared to that I was a 3rd year bachelor-student when on exchange.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The style was quite the same with lectures and student participation however, as I noted before, some of the classes were very superficial and not that specific.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
- Contemporary Ecological and Anti-Capitalist Politics
- Co-operatives, Food and Rural Sustainability
- Environmental Economics: The Problem of Climate Change
- Environmental Geographies
- Sustainable cities and communities
- Introduction to French: Complete Beginners

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I would most of all definitely recommend 'Contemporary Ecological and Anti-Capitalist Politics'! I loved this class and its content was super interesting, thorough and radical. Laurence Davis, the lecturer, was super dedicated and and an excellent lecturer. If you're interested in anti-capitalism and radical ecologism then this course is definitely for you! :) 

I also really like the content of 'Co-operatives, Food and Rural Sustainability'. However, the classes were sadly not that exciting to be honest. The lecturer was super sweet but the lectures were not that revitalizing to be honest. I still liked the course and its themes.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: No unexpected costs just more costs than when living in Copenhagen. Not because Cork is more expensive - I think overall Cork is a bit cheaper than Copenhagen. I just spend more money because I went more on excursions and trips (which I would recommend!).

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Groceries etc is cheaper however, coffee and drinks (luxury goods) are almost the same. Public transport is way cheaper than in Denmark so that was reealy lovely. But as mentioned a couple of times now, the housing crisis is critical and therefore it is really difficult to find cheap housing.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There were many different clubs and societies which was really lovely!

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Many different options. Everything from sports to cultural activities. I joined the socialist party-society, the squash club (for a bit) and the mountaneering clubm which was really cool!

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
The mountaneering club was really lovely since I got to see some beautiful mountains when going on hikes with them. 
I also liked to join the socialist society (I was there for a bit), they were very sweet people.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Go see the country's amazing nature! The mountains in the western part are stunning and so beautiful! I would definitely recommend people to go on hikes and weekend-trips. I also really liked Glengariff. It is quite turisty in the main season but i went there with friends on November and there it was super quiet which was lovely. There is a beautiful forest and coast-line.
The Dingle-peninsula is gorgeous! Go there for some days!
I also really loved Killarney national park. Go se the nature in the national park (not the actual town itself) - it is beautiful and very close to Cork. 

There are many lovely and cozy pubs in Cork: Sin É, the Friary, Roundy's and the Abbey Tavern.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer:
Very easy - the culture is in some ways not far from the danish. However, Irish culture is way more welcoming and including (in my opinion)! I had the super heartwarming experience of feeling so welcome and having many spontaneous and lovely talks with strangers (which sometimes seems impossible on Copenhagen God knows why!!) 
In classes there is maybe not that much chitchat with other students - it happens most at clubs, societies and especially in pubs!

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Explore the clubs, societies and pubs! :)

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Sometimes it was a bit difficult to connect with Irish people in my age - but that is something one would also know from Denmark.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The kind, warm and including culture of Irish people. The hospitality as well!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) Go see Irish nature - the country is absolutely beautiful! Go on weekend trips and excursions - many of my most dear memories are from trips in the country. 
2) Cork is a lovely city - try different things! It is a small city compared to Copenhagen and it is maybe not that picturesque however, the athmosphere was lovely. Go see the pubs - there you can find a cozy vibe. And check out the film festival in the city (in October I think) which was very lovely. 
3) Whatever you do, do it with your heart. You don't have to do everything and go to all clubs and societies and so on. I also liked to spend more time on my own - it is all about that balance.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: The paperwork is a lot in the beginning but everything will work out! Don't stress it, I barely remember it now. Do not hesitate reaching out for help at the exchange offices in Copenhagen and Cork - they are there to help you. :)

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting people from Irland and all over the world. The connections with people and new friendships. Seeing the beautiful nature of Ireland!

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Missing my friends and family.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Enjoy with all your heart if you're going to Cork! I already miss it now.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
